title: Strategy and tactics
summary: Experiences where players plan around constrained resources, positioning, timing, information, or asymmetric roles before committing to an outcome.

designKnowledge.playerPromise: A player can understand a problem, form a plan, and see how the plan and opponent choices changed the result.
designKnowledge.decisionQuality: Each meaningful option should have a legible cost, distinct use case, and counterplay. Randomness may create uncertainty but should not obscure why an outcome occurred.
designKnowledge.multiplayer: Specify turn order or real-time authority, disconnect handling, late join behavior, rematch reset, and any hidden information before implementation.
designKnowledge.artAndAnimation: Board state, unit range, target priority, damage, and turn ownership must remain readable on touch screens and at the camera's zoomed-out scale.
productRisks: long turns with no meaningful participation
network ordering changing the declared rules

technicalPatterns.name: Resolve authoritative turns from validated intents
technicalPatterns.guidance: Clients send bounded action intents; the server checks phase, owner, target, cost, and cooldown before applying a deterministic state transition.

technicalPatterns.name: Separate rules from presentation
technicalPatterns.guidance: Keep state transitions and balance parameters testable without requiring animation playback or UI timing.

dependencies.rationale: Collection progression can provide a roster or deck, while tactical rules determine how the collection changes decisions.
A reusable tactical card mechanic can realize one strategy subgenre without constraining the whole family.

failureModes.description: One unit, card, or opening plan makes the remaining decisions irrelevant.
failureModes.mitigation: Track outcomes by strategy and scenario, then add meaningful counters or redesign the choice set rather than hiding the dominant option.

failureModes.description: Clients show different turn results after simultaneous actions or a disconnect.
failureModes.mitigation: Resolve state on the server, version each phase, and test simultaneous requests, retries, and reconnects.

scenarios.action: Exercise each legal and illegal action in every relevant game phase.
scenarios.expected: The server accepts only actions permitted by the current state and records the same result for all clients.

scenarios.action: Play a representative turn on a touch-sized viewport without relying on hover.
scenarios.expected: Players can identify the active turn, target, cost, range, and resolved outcome.

acceptanceCriteria: Every core choice changes a legible state or resource.
Illegal, stale, and replayed requests are rejected server-side.
A new player can identify whose turn it is and why an action is legal.

considerations: Bound board and effect complexity to a measured mobile profile.
Keep UI refresh work proportional to changed state rather than rebuilding the entire board every frame.

sourceRefs.title: Approved Lab game-family and hybrid scope

evidence.description: Structured tactical design and server-authority guidance with repeatable rule and device scenarios.

assumptions: The family may be turn-based or real-time; the specific brief must choose and document the resolution model.
A balanced experience requires measured player outcomes and independent playtest review.
